title: Incremental tenant feature derivation & lookup mart
creator: Liam Chen
description:
Problem: Console dashboards and alerting depend on a series of ad-hoc joins across invocation events, route metadata, and model variant manifests. Current nightly denorm tables are slow to backfill and expensive to recompute; real-time features (e.g. recent invocation rates, cold-start counts) are stale for >12h, which harms SLO diagnosis and feature-backed cost insights.

Proposal: Build a narrow, incremental 'tenant_feature_lookup_mart' that stores precomputed feature vectors and lightweight lookup keys per tenant+route+model_variant. The mart will be append-merge (Delta/Iceberg use case) with hourly compaction and per-partition TTL. It is designed for low-latency reads by Console and for downstream rollups used by billing, SLO, and anomaly detection.

Schema (column examples):
- tenant_id STRING (partition column)
- route_id STRING (partitioned by route_id, bucketed)
- model_variant STRING
- window_start TIMESTAMP (hourly)
- invocation_count BIGINT
- successful_count BIGINT
- avg_latency_ms DOUBLE
- coldstart_count BIGINT
- kv_cache_hit_rate DOUBLE
- avg_input_tokens DOUBLE
- derived_flags STRING (comma-separated low-cardinality flags)
- last_seen TIMESTAMP
- version STRING (mart schema version)

Storage & partitioning: Use Iceberg/Delta with hourly partitions on window_start and tenant_id for efficient tenant-scoped queries. We will include a route_id hash bucket to avoid small-files explosion for high cardinality tenants. Compact hourly files nightly to control file count.

Incremental strategy:
- Source: stream of canonical invocation events (Kafka) + enrichment stream (route metadata, variant manifests).
- Ingest: Flink streaming job writes incremental merges to Iceberg using merge-on-key (tenant_id, route_id, model_variant, window_start).
- Dedup: Use event_id watermark and last_seen > window_start dedup semantics; late-arriving tolerance 30m.
- Materialization: Continuous upserts with hourly snapshots exported to a read-optimized view for Console.

Backfill & migration:
- Backfill plan uses parallel Spark job that reads historical invocation logs and builds hourly windows into the mart. Backfill will run at 4x parallelism with throttling to avoid DDL contention.
- Migration: Gradually switch Console read paths to new mart via feature flag with canary group (10% of workspaces) for 48h; validate counts against current nightly denorms.

Trade-offs considered:
- Denormalized wide tables vs narrow lookup mart: we choose a narrow mart to keep compute cost lower and to allow targeted compaction; denorm tables are cheaper for specific analytical queries but more expensive to maintain incrementally.
- Real-time freshness vs cost: hourly windows chosen as compromise between timeliness for SLO/alerts and storage/ingest cost.

Acceptance criteria:
- End-to-end job produces hourly partitions with <2% divergence vs baseline nightly for batch metrics after stabilization.
- Console dashboard query latency for tenant-scoped lookups <200ms p99 from read view.
- Backfill completes for last 90 days without schema drift errors.
- Monitoring alerts for >10% drop in ingested window counts.

Observability & validation:
- Expose metrics from Flink job: records_in, upserts_success, late_events, commit_latency.
- Data quality checks via Great Expectations: null rate thresholds, monotonicity of window_start, unique key counts.

Migration checklist:
1) Deploy mart ingestion in parallel (read-only) and run 7-day shadow compare.
2) Run backfill for 90 days.
3) Flip 10% canary reads in Console; run diff queries and SLA tests.
4) If pass, increase to 50% then 100% over 72h.
5) Deprecate old denorm exports and reclaim storage.

Security & access: Mart tables will inherit tenant-level ACLs; all reads from Console occur through service account with column-level masking for PII columns. security_review_required: true.

Rollout risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Small-file churn for high-cardinality tenants -> Mitigation: route_id bucketing + nightly compaction job.
- Risk: Late-arriving events skew hourly counts -> Mitigation: 30m lateness window + backfill reconciliation job.
- Risk: Query performance regression -> Mitigation: create read-optimized materialized view and ensure indices on (tenant_id, route_id, window_start).

Notes on cost: Expect incremental storage growth approx 50GB/week at current traffic; ingestion CPU cost estimated at 0.8 vCPU-hours per million invocations.

2026-02-25 - Priya Nair (Data Eng reviewer): Requested Great Expectations checks and idempotent backfill runs. Noted potential schema evolution problems with derived_flags. Action: add version column and migration script.

2026-03-08 - Olivia Park (Console PM): Canary plan approved. Will enable 10% canary after 7-day shadow compare. PM asked for dashboard to compare mart vs nightly denorm counts per tenant.
2026-03-12 - Ava Patel: Began 7-day shadow run. Early diffs show <1.3% variance on invocation_count for top-100 tenants. Next: run full 90-day backfill and create validation dashboard.
